article.articleTextExcerpt: The Municipal Corporation (MC) has terminated the three-year mechanical sweeping contract awarded to Karnal-based private firm Akanksha Enterprises, flagging major lapses. The project costed Rs 11.76 crore. Confirming this to The Tribune, MC Commissioner Pooja Syal Grewal said the company failed to meet prescribed coverage targets and violated operational norms. It also failed to provide quality machines according to laid down specifications and fell short of the manpower required to meet targets. An internal review based on GPS tracking revealed that the firm was covering less than 20 per cent of the targeted road length of 910 kilometres. The calculation of road length is based on a 10-foot width and the coverage capacity of a mechanical sweeping machine. If a road’s width is 20 feet, the length doubles, as a single machine covers a width of 10 feet. Internal findings indicated that the machines were required to operate at speeds of at least 8 km per hour for effective dust collection, but GPS records showed they were operating at lower speeds. article.postedBy: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates

article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. The Mumbai Monorail is India’s first and only monorail, running 19.54 km between Chembur and Sant Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle) under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), serving eastern and central Mumbai neighbourhoods that the metro and suburban rail do not reach directly. During the season, around 10 districts of the state — Kinnaur, Una, Bilaspur, Kullu, Chamba, Kangra, Mandi, Shimla, Sirmaur and Solan — received normal rainfall, while Hamirpur and Lahaul and Spiti received less rain than normal. The Centre’s data revealed that the state recorded a 36 per cent rainfall deficit in June, receiving 64.9 mm of rain against the normal 101.1 mm. During the month, only three districts — Shimla, Una and Kinnaur — received normal rainfall, while the remaining nine districts received below-average rainfall. article.articleTextExcerpt: The four-day Gugga Mari fair has been organised in the quaint town of Subathu in Solan district for decades, bringing together people belonging to various communities. Celebrated in September, 15 days after the festival of Janmashtami every year, this fair has been designated as a district-level festival. The fair is attributed to Gugga Jaharveer, also known as Gogaji or Jahar Peer, a revered folk warrior-hero and snake-god in Northern India and draws devotees from across the region. A 11th-century Chauhan Rajput ruler and warrior from Dadrewa in Churu district of Rajasthan, he was known to be a devoted follower of Guru Gorakhnath. Recognised as a Syncretic Symbol, he is revered by both Hindus and Muslims as a secular, cross-communal saint. According to the folklore of Rajasthan, Gugga had ruled a small kingdom of Dadrewa (in present day Rajasthan). According to a belief, Gugga was born with the blessings of Guru Gorakhnath, who gave ‘Gugal’ fruit to his mother Bachhal, hence came the name Gugga. article.description: The Union Government has launched India’s first Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) powered diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) train with eight coaches from Sabarmati railway station...
article.articleTextExcerpt: The Union Government has launched India’s first Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) powered diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) train with eight coaches from Sabarmati railway station to Mahesana Junction in Gujarat as part of its green initiatives on September 27, 2026. The train is based on a diesel-LNG dual fuel system for operating its driving power cars (DPCs) on both diesel and LNG. This system lets LNG to substitute for about 40 per cent of diesel usage and a full tank of LNG can operate for around 1,600 km. Moreover, two DPCs with each having 1,400 horsepower (hp) of capacity has been transformed to function using this dual fuel system with LNG tank attached to each for holding 2,200 litres of LNG. Besides, field trials for these two DPCs have also been conducted on over 2,000 km to check its reliability.

According to the Meerut police, the incident took place in the Lohianagar area. The woman, identified as Sunita, allegedly confronted her husband Mayank after finding him with Mahi Verma. As Mayank allegedly tried to drive away, Sunita climbed onto the bonnet of the car in an attempt to stop him. He allegedly continued driving with her clinging to the bonnet before locals intervened. A video of the dramatic incident later went viral on social media. Circle Officer Sangram Singh said police arrested Mayank and Mahi Verma and seized the white Toyota car. Subedar Major Satyawan's son, brother and nephew and the ambulance driver died in the accident. Gaurav Singh (28), son of the soldier, and the ambulance driver, Jaspal (30), died on the spot, while Rajan Chaudhary (35), the soldier's brother, and nephew Ram Samujh Singh (40) succumbed to their injuries during treatment at a hospital in Pithla-Kumarganj in Ayodhya district, police said. According to police, the ambulance went out of control and rammed into a truck parked on the side of the road. The impact severely damaged the ambulance. article.articleTextExcerpt: The Sri Krishna Janmasthan Sewa Sansthan in Mathura will introduce an advanced computerised testing machine to determine the purity of metal donations received at the temple, as part of the measures to bring greater transparency to the donation process. Sewa Sansthan Secretary Kapil Sharma said on Friday that the machine can test the presence of 20 different metals and will become operational from Navratri, which begins on October 11. "The purity test will be conducted in the presence of the devotee, who will be given a copy of the test report along with the donation receipt," Sharma said. The donor will have to sign the report, which will also carry the devotee's mobile phone number. A copy of the report will be preserved in the archives of the Sewa Sansthan, he said. "The machine will not require breaking the metal and can test its purity in its original form," Sharma said. He said all metal donations received in hundis or donation boxes will be tested during the counting process under CCTV surveillance and in accordance with the prescribed procedure for counting donations. I was happy to have him with me, but underneath I was worried. What if I did not perform well? What if my anxiety spoiled the journey for him? But Bhopal slowly took my mind elsewhere. We reached Bhopal and the first thing we noticed was how clean and orderly the station was. There was a sweetness in the way people spoke and lived their lives. It made me slow down. Then came the food. Hot poha, jalebi, dhokla, Bhopali paan and Bhopali chai. article.title: Stamp duty in Ghaziabad 2026: registry charges, the women’s discount and UP’s new registration rules
article.description: Stamp duty in Ghaziabad for 2026: rates, registry charges, the women's discount up to ₹1 crore, Aadhaar-based registration rules, NOCs and worked cost examples.
article.articleTextExcerpt: Stamp duty in Ghaziabad is the largest cost of buying a home after the price itself. Mahadevaswamy, Chairman & Managing Director (CMD), NBCC (India) Limited and Sh. Anjeev Jain, Director (Finance), NBCC India Limited. The project is being supported under the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative of Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC). The MoU was signed by Dr. Amit Jain, President, International Divya Parivar Society (IDPS), and Shri Rajeev Kumar, CGM (Engg.) & SBG Head, NBCC, marking an important step towards the development of this landmark cultural institution at Gurugram.
